reference.title: ‘I’ll never forget you’
reference.text: Steve Smith from Devon met Carmen Ruiz-Perez from Spain 17 years ago in Torbay, where she was studying English. They got engaged, but Carmen moved to France and the relationship ended. Steve sent a letter to her mother’s address in Spain, but it fell down behind the fireplace and stayed there for ten years.

reference.text: 17 years ago (= 17 years before now), a year after the engagement (= one year later than it), a few years later, for ten years (= during ten years).

reference.title: will / won’t / shall
rows: I won’t stay for dinner. I think I’ll go home early.
I’ll help you with your homework. Shall I open the window?
I’ll always love you. I won’t tell anybody.

reference.title: Instant decisions, offers, promises
reference.text: Use will / won’t + infinitive for decisions you make at the moment of speaking, offers and promises: I’ll have the fish. I’ll carry that for you. I’ll call you tonight.

reference.wrong: I help you with those bags.
reference.right: I’ll help you with those bags.
reference.why: For an offer, use will, not the present simple.

reference.title: Shall I / we…?
reference.text: For an offer as a question, use Shall I / we + infinitive: Shall I pay? Shall we do the washing-up?

reference.title: Stress in two-syllable verbs
reference.text: Most two-syllable verbs are stressed on the second syllable (deCIDE, forGET). Some common verbs are stressed on the first (OFfer, BORrow, HAPpen).

tasks.instruction: Ask and answer. Give examples or reasons
tasks.note: SB 4d + рамка Giving examples and reasons → разговор с ИИ

exercises.situation: Speaking practice in an English class (level: pre-intermediate), topic verb + back. Ask the student these questions one at a time and answer theirs: 1 When someone leaves you a message on your phone, do you usually call them back immediately? 2 If you buy something online that isn’t exactly what you wanted, do you always send it back? 3 Have you ever lent somebody money and they didn’t pay you back? 4 When you come back after a holiday do you usually feel better or worse than before? 5 When you borrow something from a friend, do you usually remember to give it back? 6 If you buy something to wear from a shop and then decide you don’t like it, do you usually take it back? Encourage the student to give examples and reasons (For example,… For instance,… I usually… because… It depends. When…, I usually…).
exercises.goal: Answer the questions about verb + back with examples and reasons.
exercises.opener: When someone leaves you a message on your phone, do you usually call them back immediately?
criteria: answers each question with an example or a reason
uses at least four verb + back phrases correctly (call back, send back, pay back, give back, take back, come back)
puts a pronoun between the verb and back (call them back, give it back)
uses For example / It depends / because

steps.example: It depends. When it’s my boss, I usually call him back immediately.
Yes. For example, last month I sent back a jacket because it was too small.
